module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 965

For every 2-coloring of ℝ, is there an uncountable set $A ⊆ ℝ$ such that
all sums $a + b$ for $a, b ∈ A, a ≠ b$ have the same colour?

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/965](https://www.erdosproblems.com/965)
- [Er75b] Erdős, Paul, Problems and results in combinatorial number theory. Journées Arithmétiques de Bordeaux (Conf., Univ. Bordeaux, Bordeaux, 1974) (1975), 295-310.
- [HLS17] Hindman, Neil and Leader, Imre and Strauss, Dona, Pairwise sums in colourings of the reals. Abh. Math. Semin. Univ. Hambg. (2017), 275--287.
- [Ko16] Komjáth, Péter, A certain 2-coloring of the reals. Real Anal. Exchange (2016), 227--231.
- [SWCol] Sokoup Dániel and Weiss, William, Sums and Anti-Ramsey Colourings of ℝ. https://danieltsoukup.github.io/academic/finset_colouring.pdf
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos965

/--
Erdős asks in [Er75b] if for every 2-coloring of ℝ, there is an uncountable set $A ⊆ ℝ$ such that
all sums $a + b$ for $a, b ∈ A, a ≠ b$ have the same colour.

In [Ko16] Péter Komjáth constructed a counterexample.
The same result was proven independently in [SWCol] by Sokoup and Weiss.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 3 5,
  formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/dfe2d78128b493c572cf525b1b8edf4897fb7664/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos965.lean#L42"]
theorem erdos_965 :
    answer(False) ↔ ∀ f : ℝ → Fin 2, ∃ A : Set ℝ, ¬ A.Countable ∧
      ∀ᵉ (a ∈ A) (b ∈ A) (c ∈ A) (d ∈ A), a ≠ b → c ≠ d → f (a + b) = f (c + d) := by
  sorry

/--
For every 2-coloring of ℝ, is there some $k ≥ 2$ and an uncountable set $A ⊆ ℝ$ such that all
sums $a_1 + \cdots + a_k$ of $k$ distinct elements of $A$ have the same colour?

In fact, in both [Ko16] and [SWCol] a single 2-coloring of ℝ is constructed such that for every
$k ≥ 2$ and every uncountable $A ⊆ ℝ$ the sums of $k$ distinct elements of $A$ are not
monochromatic.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 3 5]
theorem erdos_965.variants.generalization : answer(False) ↔
    ∀ f : ℝ → Fin 2, ∃ k ≥ 2, ∃ A : Set ℝ, ¬ A.Countable ∧ ∀ s t : Finset ℝ,
      ↑s ⊆ A → ↑t ⊆ A → s.card = k → t.card = k → f (s.sum id) = f (t.sum id) := by
  sorry

end Erdos965

reformulations.difference: Erdős's original statement on p. 305 asks for a set of cardinality ℵ₁; Lean asks for an uncountable set.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every set of cardinality ℵ₁ is uncountable. Conversely, every uncountable set contains an ℵ₁-sized subset, and monochromaticity of distinct pair sums is preserved under taking subsets. The equivalence for each coloring was proved in Review965.uncountable_pairMono_iff_aleph_one in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: Soukup–Weiss Corollary 3.2 asserts the existence of one coloring for which every uncountable set and every k ≥ 2 have k-element sums realizing both colors. Lean encodes this as answer(False) ↔ every coloring admits some k ≥ 2 and an uncountable set with monochromatic k-element sums.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The fixed False answer negates the entire universal assertion. Classical quantifier duality therefore gives one coloring that defeats every permitted k and every uncountable A, not a separate coloring for each k. Finsets of cardinality k encode exactly k distinct summands. For Fin 2, non-monochromaticity is equivalent to realizing both colors. This full equivalence was proved in Review965.generalization_answer_iff_soukup_weiss in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

sources_consulted: P. Erdős, Problems and results in combinatorial number theory (1975), p. 305: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1975-30.pdf
N. Hindman, I. Leader and D. Strauss, Pairwise sums in colourings of the reals, §§1 and 3; arXiv abstract and LaTeX source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.02500 and https://arxiv.org/e-print/1505.02500v1
D. T. Soukup and W. Weiss, Sums and Anti-Ramsey Colourings of ℝ, especially Lemma 2.1, Theorem 3.1 and Corollary 3.2: https://danieltsoukup.github.io/academic/finset_colouring.pdf
D. T. Soukup, publication list and description of the Soukup–Weiss notes: https://danieltsoukup.github.io/academic/pub.xhtml

Linked formal proof at commit dfe2d78128b493c572cf525b1b8edf4897fb7664: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plby/lean-proofs/dfe2d78128b493c572cf525b1b8edf4897fb7664/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos965.lean; also its nine Erdos965 dependency modules: Countability, CriticalPair, UniformPrefix, CoordinateNormalize, CylinderSplit, FiniteColoring, DeltaSystem, HamelTransfer and FiniteMain.
review.notes: Both declarations faithfully state the cited mathematics, and both negative answers and solved tags are supported by Soukup–Weiss. Lean checks covered countability, empty and singleton sets, existence of k-element subsets of uncountable sets, the k = 2 specialization, common-color versus pairwise-equality formulations, and answer polarity. The linked formal proof and its dependency closure compiled after flattening into isolated sections; #print axioms reported only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The live erdosproblems.com page was blocked by Cloudflare, and Komjáth's publisher/author copies were inaccessible. The mathematical claims were independently verified using Erdős's original paper, the HLS preprint and the directly cited Soukup–Weiss paper, which also records Komjáth's independent result.
